title: have got: body parts & symptoms
grammarNote: HAVE GOT используется для описания: 1) ВНЕШНОСТИ (цвет глаз, волос, рост); 2) СИМПТОМОВ болезни; 3) ВЛАДЕНИЯ чем-либо. Форма совпадает с Present Perfect по написанию, но используется как обычное настоящее время — 'у меня есть'. Не путай с Present Perfect!

grammarTable.example: I've got brown eyes. · I've got a headache.

rows.example: I've got a red rash — I think I'm allergic to something.
She's got food poisoning from the street food.
They've both got swollen ankles after the hiking trip.
She's got = She has got. Possession/description.
She's = She is. Job/identity — NOT have got!
have got = possession of a condition.
be + adjective: She is sick / tired / well.
Possession of people/things → have got ✅
Age → always use 'be', never 'have got'.
✅ She has got a fever. (3rd person → has got)
✅ I've got a headache. (have/has got, not am got!)
✅ He is 20 years old. (Age uses 'be', not 'have got')
✅ Are you hungry? (feelings use 'be', not 'have got')

grammarTip:
Три способа запомнить have got:
① Для ВЛАДЕНИЯ: I've got a car. · She's got two dogs. · They've got a problem.
② Для ВНЕШНОСТИ: He's got blue eyes. · She's got long hair. · I've got a scar.
③ Для СИМПТОМОВ: I've got a headache. · She's got a fever. · He's got food poisoning.

❗ НЕ используй have got для:
• ВОЗРАСТА: I am 20 years old. (не 'I've got 20 years'!)
• ЧУВСТВ: I am hungry/tired. (не 'I've got hungry'!)
• ДЕЙСТВИЙ: I have breakfast at 7. (не 'I've got breakfast'!)

exercises.text: She ___ dark hair and beautiful blue eyes.
I ___ a terrible headache — I can't concentrate on anything.
She ___ a cough — just a sore throat.
"He have got a fever" is correct.
exercises.hint: He → has got (not "have got"). Correct: He has got a fever.
Age uses "be"! I am 20 years old. (NEVER "I've got 20 years")

exercises.text: ___ you got an appointment with the doctor?
exercises.hint: You → Have you got? (not "Do you got?" or "Has you?")

exercises.text: Has Amir got a temperature? — Yes, he ___.
exercises.hint: Short answer to Has...? → Yes, he has. / No, he hasn't.

exercises.instruction: Which sentence uses have got correctly?
opts: I've got hungry after the lecture.
He's got a swollen ankle from training.
They've got tired after the exam.
exercises.correct: He's got a swollen ankle from training.
exercises.hint: "swollen ankle" = physical symptom → have got ✅. Age and feelings use "be".

questions.text: She ___ a sore throat and a high fever.
I ___ a blocked nose and I can't breathe properly.
"He have got a fever" — what is wrong?
"I've got 22 years old" is correct English.
questions.hint: Age uses "be": I am 22 years old. Never "have got" with age.

questions.text: ___ Kamila got any allergies? — No, she ___.
questions.hint: Kamila = She → Has she got? Short answer: No, she hasn't.

questions.text: They both ___ food poisoning from the street stall.
"Have you got a pen?" and "Do you have a pen?" have the same meaning.
questions.hint: have got = have. Both questions are identical in meaning.

questions.text: "She is tired" — can you rewrite this with "have got"?
questions.hint: Feelings → be: She is tired. (NOT "She's got tired"!)

questions.text: Dr. Nurova ___ brown eyes and short dark hair.
Choose the correct negative: "He ___ any pain in his chest."

questions.hint: He / She / It → has got. All others → have got.

questions.text: "She's got dark hair" uses have got for appearance.
questions.hint: have got can describe appearance: hair colour, eye colour, etc.

questions.text: I ___ a prescription from the doctor for two medicines.
Translate: "У неё жар и заложенный нос."
opts: She has got a fever and a blocked nose.
She is got fever and blocked nose.
She have got a fever and blocked nose.
She got a fever and a blocked nose.
questions.correct: She has got a fever and a blocked nose.

questions.hint: Age always uses "be": I am 20. (never "I've got 20 years")
